rejected.title: Camera shots and angles
card: Close-up
The camera is very near a face or object. It lets the viewer see small details, such as a tear, so it often shows emotion.
Long shot
The camera is far away and shows a whole place or a small figure in it. It shows the setting and how big or empty it is.
Low angle
The camera looks up at a person from below. This can make them seem powerful, strong or scary.
High angle
The camera looks down at a person from above. This can make them seem small, weak or alone.
rejected.remember: Shot size shows what we notice. Angle can shape how powerful someone seems.

a.q: A film shows a girl from high above as she stands in a big hall. What effect does this camera angle have?
opts: It makes her seem small and weak
It makes her seem strong and in charge
It shows the tear on her cheek in detail
It shows her face from very close up
a.why: The camera looks down on the girl, which is a high angle, so it can make her seem small and weak. A low angle would do the opposite and make her seem powerful. A tear or her face up close would need a close-up.
a.clue: Think about where the camera is placed compared with the girl.

b.q: In a film, Kai arrives at a huge farm. The camera is far away, so he is a tiny figure beside endless paddocks. What does this shot mainly show?
opts: The size and setting of the farm
The sadness on Kai's face
That Kai is a powerful leader
The small details of Kai's hands
b.why: A long shot is taken from far away, so it shows the setting and how big it is. Kai's face and hands would need a close-up. Power would be shown by a low angle, not by distance.
b.clue: Ask how far the camera is from Kai, and what it can fit in.
